alignments.note: Connective δέ opening the verse, rendered by the ASV's initial and.
Indefinite τις as one.
Partitive ἐξ realized by of; rule 36 keeps the English preposition with the Greek preposition rather than folding it into the pronoun.
Genitive pronoun as you.
Subjunctive εἴπῃ as the lexical verb say; the subject one belongs to τις, and the conditional if of this clause stands back in 2:15.
Dative αὐτοῖς with its case preposition unto riding along under rule 21, headed on the pronoun.
Imperative Ὑπάγετε as Go.
Preposition ἐν as in.
Anarthrous εἰρήνῃ as peace; rule 21 leaves the determinerless noun alone.
Passive imperative rendered be ye warmed; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb rather than the copula or the supplied subject pronoun.
Coordinating καί between the two imperatives.
χορτάζεσθε as filled; the copula be and subject ye of the coordinated pair stay with θερμαίνεσθε, where the ASV wrote them.

Adversative δέ rendered by the two-word connective and yet; no other source token competes for either word, s011 καί having already taken t014, and rule 2 offers no smaller defensible split. Headed on yet, the word carrying the adversative force of δέ; a head on and is defensible as the plain conjunction gloss, but rule 17 refuses a token chosen merely because it stands first.
Subjunctive δῶτε with its inflection-licensed subject pronoun under rules 7 and 9; headed on the lexical verb give.
Second αὐτοῖς as the bare object them, the ASV writing no preposition here — unlike s004, where it supplies unto.
Ordinary negative μή as not, discontinuous from its verb under rule 15; rules 41 and 59 do not bear on it, no negative indefinite standing in the clause.

Substantival article before an adjective: rule 49 makes the supplied nominal things the article's own, since an adjective cannot carry the determiner, exactly as τὸ τρίτον → the third part gives the part to the article. Rule 22 heads the unit on the nominal word rather than on the determiner.
ἐπιτήδεια as the bare adjective needful; its separation from the article's the things is ASV word order only, and rule 58 does not apply since an article is present.
Genitive article with the case preposition to riding along under rule 21, headed on the.
σώματος as body; the determiner and its case preposition belong to the article under rule 21.

Interrogative τί as what. Variant SBLGNT.JAS.2.16.v015 is underdetermined and the projection's r00-base reading is among those the English permits, so rule 97 does not apply and rule 12 forbids reopening it.

Verbless τί ὄφελος recast as what doth it profit: the predicate noun carries the supplied verb and subject pronoun under rules 68 and 96, and rule 17 heads the unit on profit, the word glossing ὄφελος.

review_notes: Reviewed unchanged: no unit was altered. Every s### and t### id is partitioned exactly once; 22 source and 31 target tokens accounted for, and every unit is aligned with both heads members of their arrays.

s015 δέ takes both t016 and and t017 yet: s011 καί has already taken t014, no other source token can license either word, and rule 2 offers no smaller defensible split. The head choice between and and yet is the one materially contested point in the verse and is recorded in the unit note; rule 17's refusal of a token chosen merely for standing first is what settles it on yet.

s017 τά follows rule 49's adjective clause — the supplied nominal things is the article's own, since ἐπιτήδεια cannot carry the determiner — rather than being left unrepresented under rule 23. Rule 22 then keeps the head on things and not on the. This is the τὸ τρίτον → the third part shape.
s013 μή is an ordinary negative aligned to not; rules 41, 59 and 79 are not in play, there being no negative indefinite in the clause and no verb of denial.

s004 and s016 are the same dative pronoun analysed two ways because the ASV writes unto for the first and a bare object for the second; the case preposition rides with the pronoun under rules 21 and 36 rather than being split off or left unrepresented.

s022's supplied doth it goes to the predicate noun rather than to τί: rule 68 gives a supplied subject and verb to the predicate where the clause expresses no subject of its own, and rule 96 keeps them there. A reading that gave doth it to the interrogative would have to read the supplied verb off English word order, which rule 63 refuses.
